q1.q: Be honest: why are you really thinking about leaving?
q1.a: I want more energy and culture: bold art, busy streets and a city with something new to discover every day.
q1.b: I want to slow right down — somewhere warm by the sea, where life moves at an easier pace.
q1.c: I want more space, fewer distractions and enough calm to think clearly again.
q1.d: I want to feel more connected to the people, place and daily life around me.

q2.q: You've just arrived in a new city. What do you do first?
q2.a: Head to the busiest market or neighbourhood and explore whatever catches my attention.
q2.b: Head straight for the beach, kick off my shoes and take a moment to breathe.
q2.c: Look for the nearest trail, forest or peaceful edge of town.
q2.d: Speak to a long-time resident and ask where I should go to understand the place properly.

q3.q: A friend asks what you're looking for abroad. You say...
q3.a: Somewhere full of culture, art and events I can take part in.
q3.b: Somewhere warm and coastal, with slow mornings and no pressure to rush.
q3.c: Somewhere peaceful and surrounded by nature, with plenty of room to be alone.
q3.d: Somewhere I can belong, build close relationships and become part of a neighbourhood.

q4.q: What would make you feel like you'd truly made it abroad?
q4.a: I know the best local spots, always have somewhere new to go and recognise people around the neighbourhood.
q4.b: I no longer plan every hour. My days feel relaxed, open and unhurried.
q4.c: I have a favourite trail, a view I return to and a place where I can be alone.
q4.d: The café owner knows my order, I have a regular table and people know my name.

q5.q: What's the thing you're most willing to give up to live abroad?
q5.a: Predictability. I want new experiences, places and people to keep surprising me.
q5.b: Ambition, for a while. I'd trade a busy work life for more rest and freedom.
q5.c: Convenience. I'd live far from shops and services if it gave me more space and access to nature.
q5.d: Comfort and familiarity, if it helped me build stronger relationships somewhere new.

q6.q: You're having a hard week abroad, homesick, frustrated, nothing's working. What gets you through?
q6.a: I find something happening nearby, such as a market, concert or exhibition, and let the atmosphere lift me.
q6.b: I go for a swim, or sit and watch the sunset until I feel calmer.
q6.c: I take a long walk in nature and give myself time to clear my head.
q6.d: A neighbour brings food, a friend checks in or someone from my community spends time with me.

q7.q: What's your relationship with language barriers?
q7.a: I enjoy working things out as I go, even in the middle of a busy market or conversation.
q7.b: I'm comfortable communicating with simple words and gestures while I learn at my own pace.
q7.c: I'm comfortable with limited conversation because I prefer spending most of my time alone or outdoors.
q7.d: I'll learn the local language because making an effort is part of joining the community.

q8.q: Someone asks how long you're planning to stay. You say...
q8.a: As long as the place keeps giving me new things to explore. That could be 1 year or 10.
q8.b: Indefinitely, as long as life stays this unhurried and I wake up near the shore.
q8.c: As long as I still have the space, solitude and access to nature I came for.
q8.d: Indefinitely. If I build a home and community there, I won't feel the need to leave.

q9.q: Which of these would make you fall in love with a destination?
q9.a: Finding a street party by chance, joining the celebration and ending the night over dinner with new people.
q9.b: An afternoon in a hammock in the shade, salt air nearby and nothing on my schedule.
q9.c: Turning a corner and finding a vast landscape that makes me stop and take it all in.
q9.d: Seeing people I trust build lasting homes, friendships and routines there.

q10.q: Ten years from now, the version of you that made the right choice abroad...
q10.a: Still discovers new places, people and experiences, and rarely feels bored.
q10.b: Lives by the ocean, with a slower, lighter and less stressful daily life.
q10.c: Has a beautiful view, plenty of space and a peaceful life built around nature.
q10.d: Has close friends, familiar rituals and a community that feels like home.

urban.name: Urban Explorer
urban.description: You're a culture sponge. You thrive in dynamic places where the espresso is strong, the art is bold, and the possibilities feel endless. Think: bustling markets, late-night jazz clubs, walkable streets, and ten different languages in earshot. You're fuelled by curiosity, connection, and the thrill of being part of something.
urban.youllLove: Barcelona, Tokyo, Lisbon, Buenos Aires, Mexico City

coastal.name: Coastal Dreamer
coastal.description: Slow mornings. Salt on your skin. A deep need to exhale. You belong somewhere where the water is clear, the days are long, and shoes are optional. You're not trying to impress anyone — you're here to unwind, connect, and maybe learn how to surf or nap like a pro.
coastal.youllLove: Koh Phangan, Bali, Canary Islands, Tulum, Zanzibar

nature.name: Nature Seeker
nature.description: Solitude is sacred, and nature is your sanctuary. You don't mind getting your hands dirty or taking the long way around if it means peace, quiet, and epic views. You're probably a deep thinker, a good listener, and maybe even a little bit mystical.
nature.youllLove: Chiang Mai, San Cristóbal de las Casas, the Pyrenees, Oaxaca's highlands, the Dolomites

rooted.name: Rooted Romantic
rooted.description: You're all about meaningful simplicity. You value community, connection, and daily life that's grounded and slow. You don't mind hard work — especially when it's in service of something real, like growing food, raising kids, or putting down roots.
rooted.youllLove: Rural France, Southern Spain, Central Portugal, Northern Thailand, Sicily's countryside
